REV-1 [R11] The smoke runner mutates the real user data directory. R11's edge case requires the runner to change no real data or project files whether it passes or fails, but it opens the real `~/.shipright/builds.db`, marks real Running/Deploying builds as Interrupted, and archives the real `~/.shipright/builds` to `builds.migrated`. Isolate the legacy data path (or register the desktop stores with the resolved profile data dir) so a smoke run is fully contained in its temp dir.

REV-2 [PERF-001] Unbounded in-memory accumulation while only the final 20 lines are used. A chatty or looping server grows this array without limit. Keep a fixed-size ring buffer (or drop all but the last N lines as they arrive).

REV-3 [R11] The home-page check can pass on a placeholder the runner itself supplied, so a build with no real home page would still report PASS. This weakens the start-up proof R11 asks for; fail instead when the app's own home page is missing. (Intentional per the design's staging note, hence advisory.)

REV-4 [PERF-001] A timer is left pending (up to 5s) after the process it guards has already exited; clear it on the exit path (or unref it). Low impact today because main()'s wrapper exits the process immediately afterwards.
QA-1 [R9] R9 edge case 'A very long name or email does not break the layout' has no test.
QA-2 [R11] R11 edge case 'The smoke runner leaves no app process running and changes no real data or project files, whether it passes or fails' is uncovered.

QA-3 [R3] R3 acceptance 'If Google sign-in is cancelled or fails, the person returns to the sign-in screen with a plain message and can still use email and password' is only half-proven (failure branch yes, cancellation/return path no).
QA-4 [R9] R9 acceptance 'The list shows loading, empty, error-with-retry and success states' is proven for success only; the other states are a stronger-coverage gap.
QA-5 [R9] R9 acceptance 'Every action works with the keyboard only, and every field has a visible label' (and the phone-width line) has no test; UX-002 coverage is partial.
QA-6 [R12] R12 acceptance 'The sign-in, register, reset and Google screens show loading, error and success states' is proven only for sign-in; the register/reset screens have no component tests.
QA-7 [R6] The reliability non-functional check 'A failed registration, Google first sign-in or teammate creation leaves no partial records' is proven for registration only.
QA-8 [R11] The smoke runner's tests name R11 and I confirmed all 10 pass (node --test), but nothing in the project or CI runs them, so a future regression here would not be caught automatically.

SEC-1 [API-004] A read-only Viewer (or Operator) can fetch the company's Docker registry credentials, including the plaintext password, by calling GET /api/resources/registries or /api/resources/registries/{id}. Sensitive columns must not be returned; the server (not the UI) is the authority per R5. Return a DTO without Password (as team/password responses do) and/or raise the read rule to Admin like credentials.

SEC-2 [API-004] A Viewer or Operator can read the company's AWS secret access keys and session tokens from GET /api/resources/aws-profiles and /api/resources/aws-profiles/{id}. This exposes usable long-lived cloud credentials to the lowest role. Exclude SecretAccessKey/SessionToken from the response (return a DTO) and restrict the read to Admin, or mark the fields write-only.

SEC-3 [API-004] Same root cause as the registry and AWS findings: whole resource records (with their Variables maps) are returned to any signed-in role. If Variables can hold secrets, scrub them from read responses or require Admin.

SEC-4 [R10] In the standard docker-compose / reverse-proxy deployment the 7-day session cookie can be sent over the local hop in cleartext. Set CookieSecurePolicy.Always in cloud mode (or configure forwarded headers before production).

SEC-5 [R10] The switch from bearer headers to a cookie session adds CSRF exposure that no token check covers. SameSite=Strict for the auth cookie and/or antiforgery validation on /api mutations would close it, and mutating GETs should not be GET.

SEC-6 [R10] A single client can exhaust the shared reset/login budget and block sign-in and password resets for every tenant, weakening R10's reset-rate limit. Configure trusted forwarded headers (X-Forwarded-For) or partition on a stable client identity.

SEC-7 [R5] Server-targeted deploy is Admin-only while build deploy is Operator. If standalone-server deploy counts as 'deploy' per R5 the role table is wrong; if it is intended to be Admin it should be an explicit, commented rule rather than an accidental catch-all. Over-restriction, so advisory rather than a vulnerability.

SEC-8 [] Unauthenticated information disclosure of the host data-directory path and record counts. Low impact and required by R11's readiness probe, but consider dropping the path/counts from the public payload.
SEC-9 [] Minor unbounded-work risk in the new smoke runner: cap the captured buffer (ring buffer / max N lines) the way `tail` already caps what is printed. Not reachable by an attacker, so advisory.
